title: I used AI to help turn the rooms I had in my head into a game. This is where it's at now.
author: IDislikeBeingOnFire
selftext:
I've been working on my first game, The Narrator, and thought this might be a good place to share it.

I already had the rooms, layouts, colour schemes and general visual direction in mind, but I'm not an artist. 

I used generative AI to help turn those ideas into 2D visual starting points, then edited and modified the results myself to create the environments I actually use in the game.

The game itself is a comedy point-and-click exploration game where the Narrator knows he's inside a video game, reacts to what the player does, remembers their behaviour and absolutely hates both the player and me, the developer.

The writing, narration and voice acting are all my own, and there's no AI-generated content being created during gameplay. 

AI has basically been one of the tools that allowed me to actually turn the visual side of the idea I had in my head into something I could build.

I've attached the trailer because it's probably easier to show what I've ended up making than try to explain it all 

The Steam page went live this week if anyone wants to have a look

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5215880/The\_Narrator/⁠

Would be interested to hear how other people here have approached using AI-generated visuals as a starting point and then editing them for their games.

comments.author: CraigBMG
comments.body:
You game looks like it has some personality, I might need to keep an eye on that one! 😄   
  
I did a lot of concept work with local models / ComfyUI for my game [Jigsaw Diorama](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4861620/Jigsaw_Diorama_The_Alchemist_and_the_Eclipse/).    
  
I had the game running, but desperately needed some content.  I thought it would be cool to have some sort of implied story/journey to the puzzles.  
  
Z-Image did pretty well at putting together concept images, but ultimately ChatGPT Image 2 just "got" what I was trying to go for.

Most of the puzzle images have been touched up / expanded in Krita with Flux 2 Klein locally and general hand touchups.

We'll see how it goes, but I think it turned out pretty nice.  Super relaxing.  "No pressure. No drama. Just puzzle pieces."
